requirements.statement: Allow novice users to install missing Codex/Claude desktop apps and continue selected connection from Yecai without choosing binary architecture or typing commands, while preserving installed applications and truthful recovery.
acceptance: Missing desktop apps offer install and connect; non-automatic clients offer guided help with no false automatic claim. Existing apps use the current connect/open/restore path unchanged.

Native code selects compiled source/identity and OS architecture; renderer cannot provide URLs, paths, package identity, command text or elevation flags. Original packages are verified by macOS codesign/Gatekeeper or Windows signed Appx deployment and exact publisher/identity.

One native job serializes install attempts and is request-idempotent. Safe download stages support cancellation, validator-bound resume, exact size/type checking and same-package reuse; stale/malformed data and lost UI responses cannot claim completion or trigger duplicate installs.

Native re-detection before and after installation prevents overwrite/reinstall and distinguishes installed, missing runtime and external change. Installation is not account/model connection success. Failure never uninstalls user software or modifies account/model data.

Install-and-connect captures explicit account, app, model/group and line selection; auto continuation occurs at most once after fresh discovery and only if that same selection/session remains current. A changed context requires fresh confirmation.

Accessible inline progress and actionable errors survive navigation; unsigned/challenged/unsupported/permission/dependency/space/interruption cases are explicit. macOS and Windows fixture/compile results are reported separately from actual native install acceptance.

requirements.statement: Synchronize official desktop release metadata and original installer bytes privately every six hours, with recoverable bounded downloads and truthful verification status, without altering any end-user application or public release.
acceptance: Six explicitly identified official desktop source slots are configured; unsupported/blocked sources stay visible as failures rather than fabricated current versions or substituted CLI packages.

Each redirect is HTTPS, exact-host allowlisted and public-address validated; content lengths, type and validators are checked. No auth/cookies, insecure TLS, arbitrary URL fetching or execution of downloaded bytes.

Changed-only downloads support validator-bound resume; changed validators, invalid content ranges, oversized bodies, incomplete/corrupt packages and interrupted state writes cannot yield a completed candidate. Valid private cached candidates are independently hash-checked before reuse.

One lock serializes timer/manual runs. Atomic receipts preserve prior good candidates across replay, failed source lookup, disk quota, stale data and interruption. No arbitrary or automatic recursive deletion, symlink following, downgrade publication or public output.

MSIX manifest identity, architecture and version are inspected without extraction; signature-file presence is not signature trust. Native verification helper reports actual platform verification separately. Pending signatures and untested installation/compatibility never become verified or published.

Provide a hardened independent systemd timer/service at six-hour cadence, bounded download capacity configuration and secret-free status/rollback instructions; verify real first/second runs and distinguish partial upstream failure from script errors.

requirements.statement: Bootstrap the owner-provided HTTPS download/update origin without exposing secrets, interrupting existing services or pretending unsigned/unpublished releases are available.
acceptance: Only the chosen ingress host and dedicated download paths/container are added; existing ingress source bytes are preserved as an exact prefix and backed up. Reapply is idempotent; conflicting or concurrent changes stop before replacement.

Origin container is non-root, read-only, no host ports, no inherited secrets and no newly persistent access logs. Only GET/HEAD public allowlisted routes exist; hidden files, traversal, directories and unsafe methods are rejected. Public root contains no symlinks or secrets.

Public and direct-origin HTTPS verifies normally. Range request returns 206 with exact bytes and hash matches the immutable probe fixture. Original routes are observed before/after without paid or private requests.

Both updater channel endpoints return HTTP 204 with no-store until separately approved signed release publication. Health and root explicitly distinguish origin readiness from unpublished installers and inactive client auto-updates.
No private signing key, SSH password, existing app data, internal installers or third-party binaries are published. DNS, certificate, live routing and real installation limitations remain explicit.

requirements.statement: Correct full friendly model names and verified per-model reasoning controls and forwarding across existing adapters, preserving unknown-model default use and transactional connection behavior.
acceptance: Friendly labels never alter exact request, credential, or billing model IDs; picker search matches both label and ID.
Known model menus reflect verified capabilities through native schemas; unknown models expose default access without invented reasoning/image/context capabilities or new eligibility gates.

Explicit effort values reach conversion and passthrough requests correctly. GPT-6 max is not silently xhigh; DeepSeek off uses its documented toggle. Defaults do not impose maximum effort or new output budgets.

Reapplying configuration remains reversible and preserves other providers and user preferences. Existing model/group selection, in-flight route snapshots and synthetic failure/recovery tests remain passing.
Real renderer/native tests, production frontend compilation and Windows/Apple cross-compilation verify this bounded unit; no live account or installer success is claimed.

requirements.statement: Implement explicitly selected model sets with real identity and fixed per-model billing routes, honest request errors and cooperative bounded exit without packaging or server mutation.
acceptance: Up to the documented 200-entry catalog bound, unique full model IDs bind explicit billing groups; default is a member. No silent cross-group fallback or enrollment of unselected models. Legacy records upgrade on explicit activation only.

All seven adapters publish native model menus/catalogs via authenticated loopback routing; legitimate native default changes are not configuration corruption. In-flight requests retain their route. Unsupported optional vendor menus do not block default use.
Credential sets remain inside OS credential storage, handle the Windows per-blob bound transactionally, and never expose full keys through renderer, files, errors or diagnostics.

Claude identity uses real IDs rather than Sonnet display masking; both bridges route requested model exactly and isolate continuation history. Curated HTTP/SSE errors and in-memory last-request observations never turn failed streams into success.

Window close offers background/cancel/exit globally. Confirmed exit rejects new operations, cancels safe work, preserves in-flight account mutations and local rollback, and stops owned runtimes with bounded grace and recoverable progress.

Synthetic transaction/route/stream/exit tests, actual renderer tests/typecheck/build and Windows compilation pass. No installer, signed release, server change or live-account success is inferred from these tests.

requirements.statement: Repair cross-application diagnosis, platform launching, usable CLI opening and truthful verification/recovery without modifying servers or real user settings during development.
acceptance: Real Rust-serialized reachable/mixed/failure connectivity results are accepted by the renderer; stale, malformed, partial and invoke errors never invent network failures or lose valid per-line evidence.

Windows Store/MSIX discovery preserves validated package application identity; ordinary desktop executables remain supported and unsafe/unrelated launch targets are rejected. Initialization and daily opening share platform launcher.
CLI proof rejects banners/help/empty/failed output; typed process failures distinguish start, timeout, read/wait and nonzero execution; outputs/secrets never cross IPC.

All seven targets are offered launch-only opening after read-only validation; four CLI targets open a terminal using native-resolved paths without secrets or caller commands. Repeated open does not reconfigure or issue probes.
File or credential restoration failures are visible recovery-required states, never unchanged/restored success; account switch, stale reply and recovery journal boundaries remain intact.

All scoped regressions, renderer typecheck/production build and Windows compile are recorded separately from real platform/application acceptance. Internal 0.4.8 artifacts never imply complete live-user validation.

requirements.statement: Complete the 0.4.7 client hotfix with consistent source/UI/artifact version identity and current production acceptance while preserving historical evidence.
acceptance: The renderer version is derived from package.json rather than separately hardcoded. Package, Tauri, Cargo manifest and own lockfile package all equal 0.4.7.

A new version-aware production acceptance retains typechecking, hardened-runtime/updater-disabled assertions and real production asset checks; old frozen 0.4.6 acceptance files and failed RU-039 reports are not rewritten.
All current privacy/protocol native and renderer regression scenarios pass; no extra product, server, real-user or public-release scope is inferred.

requirements.statement: Remove internal upstream model descriptions from the client and preserve legitimate Claude nonstream responses without weakening activation evidence.
acceptance: Native model projection uses an empty optional-display description value; model IDs, billing groups, ratios and prices are unchanged. Raw upstream description is neither rendered nor searched on configuration and model-price pages, even from stale renderer fixtures.

Both direct Anthropic and Chat conversion paths return valid completed empty/whitespace/thinking-only messages rather than invalid-provider 502; these responses do not emit activation verification. Useful complete responses still emit exactly the existing evidence.

Real upstream HTTP errors remain errors; malformed JSON/message payloads and incomplete messages are not manufactured into success. Streaming behavior, pinned model, auth headers, bounded bodies/timeouts and no automatic extra requests remain intact.

Loopback-only synthetic proxy fixtures cover startup-shaped max_tokens:1, chat success, error and auth cases; current native/renderer regressions, typecheck and production build pass. No real secrets, configurations or paid model probes are used.

Internal 0.4.7 artifacts are distinct from retained 0.4.6, with actual signing/notarization/hash checks and explicit Windows/no-live-test limitations. No GitHub push/public release, updater or backend mutation. Explain separate public pricing-description exposure rather than claiming client redaction secures the endpoint.

requirements.statement: Prepare and deliver the approved current source and internal installers without false legacy storage failures or public-release side effects.
acceptance: Missing recovery key plus absent or lock-only directory is absence, not corruption; real/unknown recovery material remains protected and never causes key replacement. Synthetic fixtures require no real Keychain or tool configuration.
Existing native, renderer and production build regression passes without changing account, billing, activation or recovery contracts.
Source staging excludes installers and credentials. Push only the existing product branch, never v tags, Release/R2 or update manifests.

Internal macOS build is universal, Developer-ID signed, hardened and submitted for notarization; report accepted/stapled/verified only on actual tool evidence. Windows cross-built executable is explicitly unsigned and not claimed real-device verified. If a platform cannot finish, state the concrete blocker.
Record exact source identity and artifact SHA256 with known real-account and old-entry integration-test limitations. No server or public release changes.

requirements.statement: Expose official estimated charge, Yecai charge and savings together on the existing summary card using unchanged comparable-record aggregates.
acceptance: Overview and account show all three labeled amounts without opening details, using the same native aggregate without recalculation or new requests.
Official amount remains labeled as estimated; recent comparable-record basis and existing detailed caveats remain accessible. Yecai charge is not claimed to be a cash receipt.
Positive savings, genuine zero, negative difference, loading and unavailable states remain distinct. Missing amounts use three unknown placeholders, never fabricated zeros.

Shared card is readable in light/dark and narrow layouts with no clipped figures. Details action retains keyboard focus behavior. Existing frontend regression, typecheck and renderer production build pass; no new release or real-account validation claim.

requirements.statement: Display website-aligned account currency and auditable recent estimated savings without new backend privileges or invented historical totals.
acceptance: Current CNY status projects customer-facing RMB credits using quota_per_unit and usd_exchange_rate; missing/unsupported settings show unavailable, never USD or zero fallback. Cumulative consumed credits use account used_quota, not recent TPM.

Fetch only newest bounded 100 consumption records through the existing native desktop bearer and fixed first-party origin. Do not pass raw rows, metadata, credentials or user IDs into renderer IPC; failed logs do not sign out the account.

Match the website's quota, recorded special/group ratio, price and usd_exchange_rate formula for supported comparable records. Exclude malformed, non-consumption, free, subscription, special-fee and unknown basis records; both totals use the same included rows.

Keep negative savings truthful and distinguish available zero, no history, no comparable records, unavailable and refresh-stale states. Never imply recent-100-row calculations are cumulative/monthly or real cash savings.

Use a closed schema5 financial projection with finite bounded decimal strings, explicit counts and optional zero date window. Decoder preserves existing schema3/4 and rejects extra fields, impossible aggregates or signed-out finance.

Overview and account share currency/savings logic, provide concise receipt-like detail and current-rate explanation; retain actual usage as a secondary metric and clarify mainland/global network lines do not change price groups.

Run isolated native and renderer regressions, type/build, arithmetic and boundary fixtures plus local light/dark/narrow keyboard visual checks. No server changes or release/real-account validation claims.

requirements.statement: Make first setup and daily reuse simple without silent cost changes, secret exposure, lock-in or false success.
acceptance: Read-only full current-tree baseline proof before product edits; immutable historical failures/proofs.
Installed/connected apps first and missing apps expandable. Full model IDs, group ratios, comparison assumptions and restoration remain visible or accessible.

Native Open for Claude Desktop/Codex Desktop/DSH needs no account login, rewrites no settings, issues no tokens and sends no paid test. DSH reuses live process and starts on explicit Open after assistant relaunch. Opened is not a new provider-verification claim.
No arbitrary renderer paths/URLs/commands/credentials. Serialize open/restore/activation; preserve unrelated edits, reject pending recovery or changed owned provider identity.
Missing saved model/group never silently picks a replacement, even after refresh errors; explicit selection shows new price before apply.
Failure states expose relevant account, model, group, line, installation or recovery actions. Quit names affected applications and explains DSH reopening.
Closed schema4 includes billing/protocol/cache fields with unavailable optional amounts omitted not zero; legacy3 remains renderer-readable.

Native isolated regression, ordinary-account/empty-app/price-change/error/double-click renderer tests, type/build and light/dark/narrow keyboard checks. No Windows real-device or release claims without evidence.

requirements.statement: Deliver a reversible app-centered desktop workbench with resilient login and audited pricing/security corrections.
acceptance: Save one AES-GCM encrypted pre-connection baseline before configuration writes; key only in OS storage. Retain baseline through model/group switches; no history.

Local inspect and explicit restore need no login, serialize with activation, restore only owned fields by three-way comparison and preserve later edits. Invalid files are never overwritten. Interrupted operations retain recovery material and retry safely.
Legacy connections remove only identified YesChoy settings; unknown original values are not invented. No shared server tokens revoked.
Login retry survives transient errors, cancellation rejects stale results, stale signed-in data is disclosed. Navigation cannot discard ongoing setup.
Seven apps show persistent model, line, group and visible restore. Search retains full model IDs; UI receives keyboard, narrow-window, light/dark visual checks.
NewAPI cache ratios feed the shared 100-million-token estimator. Bridges refuse redirects and require completed usable replies; background-dependent connections explain lifecycle.
No server, NewAPI, DB, deployment, telemetry or updater changes. User-confirmed Windows build on another account remains independently unverified.

requirements.statement: Correct false dual-line Codex activation rollback and present a reproducible cache-heavy 100 million token official-versus-YesChoy estimate in a client-only 0.4.5 successor.
acceptance: Codex Desktop activation for either compiled line writes and reads back only the owned provider, exact model and owned catalog, validates command-backed credential loading, completes one bounded real model response through the exact selected direct Responses or loopback Chat-conversion path, and launches the selected desktop installation before returning ready.

A full general-purpose Codex agent session, unrelated plugin availability and incidental JSONL event shape are not installation gates. Real configuration, secure-storage, authentication, line, model, invalid-response and launch failures remain non-ready, restore volatile snapshots and return distinct closed reason codes without raw body, key or local path.
The loopback Codex provider supports bounded HEAD Responses and GET Models compatibility checks without exposing credentials, accepting caller-selected upstreams or listening beyond loopback.

The price panel displays one concise 100 million token cache-heavy example: 10 million new input, 80 million cache reads and 10 million output. It derives official and current-account estimates from current NewAPI billing expressions or base prices, selected billing-group ratio and positive server exchange rate.

Multiple NewAPI price tiers produce an honest min-to-max estimate rather than hidden row selection. When no separate cache-read price exists, the calculation uses the input price and says so; request-priced or unparseable models remain unavailable rather than receiving an invented estimate.

The client version advances coherently to 0.4.5. Renderer and native tests cover calculation, tier range, fallback disclosure, both Codex transports, closed failures, secret boundaries and rollback. A notarized universal macOS DMG and an explicitly unsigned Windows 10/11 x64 NSIS candidate are produced only after their applicable gates pass.

No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, server source, server database, production deployment, telemetry or automatic-updater activation is changed. Windows behavior is claimed only from Windows runner evidence, not macOS compilation alone.

requirements.statement: Make every current-account model that advertises Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Chat genuinely usable in Claude Code and Claude Desktop through evidence-driven native routing or a client-local bidirectional bridge, then produce truthful macOS and Windows 0.4.4 candidates without server mutation.
acceptance: Claude Code and Claude Desktop list a current-account model when pricing advertises anthropic or openai, hide models with neither protocol, show the exact model ID and billing group, and label native versus automatic compatibility in plain language.
Activation revalidates current account availability, billing group and endpoint metadata. It prefers native Anthropic whenever advertised and uses a local Chat bridge only for openai-only models.

The bridge converts Anthropic request bodies to OpenAI Chat, rewrites only to the exact selected model, converts non-stream and streaming responses back to Anthropic, and covers system prompts, images, tool definitions, tool calls, tool results, reasoning, usage and terminal errors using the repository's mature converter.

Claude Code and Claude Desktop use isolated loopback routes so both may remain configured simultaneously. Each complete NewAPI key stays in OS secure storage; bridged targets receive only a high-entropy local token, and outbound origins are restricted to yeschoy.com or api.yeschoy.com.

Claude Code direct activation stops an obsolete Claude Code bridge, Chat activation resumes it after helper restart, and Claude Desktop resumes its route after helper restart. Failed start, write, readback, launch or target verification restores the prior files, credential and bridge state without retained backups.

The client version advances coherently to 0.4.4. Renderer, native and release-unit tests cover routing priority, both Claude targets, secret boundaries, non-stream, stream, tools, restart, external change, replay and rollback.

A signed and notarized universal macOS DMG is verified on Apple Silicon and Intel architectures. A Windows 10/11 x64 NSIS installer is built and uploaded only after the Windows renderer and native gates pass; it is explicitly unsigned until a Windows certificate exists.

No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, server source, server database, production deployment, telemetry or automatic-updater activation is part of this change. A blocked Windows runner is reported as an external blocker rather than a successful artifact.

requirements.statement: Make account-available OpenAI-compatible models genuinely usable in Codex Desktop through evidence-driven direct Responses or a client-local Responses-to-Chat bridge, with an owned model catalog and no server mutation.
acceptance: Codex Desktop lists an account model when current pricing advertises either openai-response or openai; models without either endpoint remain hidden, and the exact model ID plus server-owned billing group stay visible.

Activation revalidates current account availability, billing group and endpoint metadata. It prefers direct Responses whenever advertised and uses a loopback-only Responses-to-Chat bridge only for openai-only models.

The local bridge converts request, non-stream response, streaming response, function tools, custom tools and previous-response tool history using the repository's mature CC Switch conversion behavior, while forwarding only to the closed selected yeschoy.com or api.yeschoy.com origin.

The complete tool key remains in OS secure storage and reaches Codex only through the signed command helper. It is absent from renderer IPC, ordinary Codex configuration, model catalogs, logs, paths and retained backup history.

One activation transaction writes the dedicated yeschoy provider and an owned model_catalog_json file, preserves unrelated Codex settings and user-owned catalogs, verifies both readbacks, launches the selected installation for a harmless real reply and restores both files plus credential on failure.

A bridged configuration resumes its loopback service when the helper app starts and does not claim readiness if the bridge cannot bind or the target-level request fails. Direct configurations do not depend on the bridge.

Renderer, native and release-unit tests cover direct priority, Chat fallback, unsupported protocols, visibility, catalog ownership, secret absence, streaming and tool conversion, restart, external change and rollback.
The client version advances coherently to 0.4.3. No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, server database, production deployment, telemetry or automatic-update activation is part of this change.

requirements.statement: Restore the verified Cloudflare origin as the single global_accelerated route in the 0.4.2 client without adding a third beginner choice or weakening session, credential, configuration and verification boundaries.
acceptance: The two selectable line IDs remain mainland_optimized and global_accelerated, mapped exactly to https://yeschoy.com and https://api.yeschoy.com in native connectivity, account origin resolution, credential validation, renderer diagnostics and configuration previews.
yeschoy.pro is not selectable, accepted as a newly written credential origin, probed by diagnostics or used as an automatic fallback; existing unrelated third-party configuration is preserved.

Changing line selection preserves the existing first-party account session and refreshes through the line that issued it. A selected route failure remains retryable and never silently mutates through another origin.
All seven tool adapters receive the selected compiled origin, retain field-owned transaction and rollback behavior, and require their target-level verification before ready.

The package version is 0.4.2 across JavaScript, Cargo, Tauri and candidate readiness, with a newly signed and notarized macOS universal package and a newly built explicitly unsigned Windows x64 candidate.
No NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, telemetry or automatic-updater mutation is part of this client change.

requirements.statement: Deliver one testable client-only release candidate with two currently usable first-party lines, truthful NewAPI-owned account and price data, and secure verified one-click setup for seven explicitly named tools while keeping the unavailable API origin and unproven updater inactive.
acceptance: The only selectable lines are mainland_optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global_accelerated at https://yeschoy.pro. api.yeschoy.com is neither selected nor health-claimed and cannot receive an automatic retry of a token or other mutating request.

Changing selectable lines preserves one valid first-party desktop session. Only logout, expiry, revocation or an authenticated authorization failure clears credentials; a route or network failure remains retryable.

Available model IDs, supported endpoint types, billing groups, group ratios, usd_exchange_rate and actual prices come from the current authenticated NewAPI responses. Missing or malformed data is unavailable, never compiled or invented.

The setup surface names Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex Desktop, Pi, DSH web, Hermes and OpenClaw separately, selects an unambiguous installation, shows exact model ID and billing group, and never gates an ordinary version string by allowlist.

Hermes and OpenClaw integrations preserve unrelated configuration and resolve their credential from the signed client helper or another non-literal operating-system-protected boundary. No complete API key crosses renderer IPC, appears in ordinary configuration, logs, diagnostics, process arguments or retained backup history.

Every supported target is ready only after readback and a harmless target-level request using the selected line, exact model and credential. Configuration-only, launch-only, direct relay probe, missing runtime, ambiguous installation, target timeout and failed response remain non-success states with recovery guidance.

Renderer and native tests cover sign-in projection consistency, line switching, group pricing, future versions, install ambiguity, configuration preservation, replay, concurrent change, rollback, secret absence and all seven tool identities.

The macOS universal and Windows x64 candidate build inputs use the branded icon and matching 0.4.x versions. The Windows artifact is explicitly unsigned. An updater is exposed only after a public update key, signed payloads, a versioned manifest and tamper/relaunch tests are present; otherwise settings truthfully describe it as unavailable.
No NewAPI, Nginx, DNS, database, server source, server deployment, telemetry upload, remote agent or public production-readiness claim is part of this client unit.

requirements.statement: Generalize installed-tool eligibility across ordinary versions without weakening identity, credential, configuration or verification boundaries.
acceptance: Unknown, future and Windows four-component version strings never gate eligibility. Missing runtime is distinct from unsupported version.
Re-resolve selected identity and check required invocation capabilities before credentials. Help probes are bounded, isolated and secret-free; no model requests on scan or help.
Failed capability checks are retryable, not proof of incompatibility. Claude Desktop remains awaiting runtime verification through its existing 3P transaction.
Preserve schema parsing, unrelated configuration, readback, external-change detection and rollback. Codex JSON startup/error output alone cannot become ready.
UI displays detected version or unread version, installed/pending verification and actionable capability errors, with no forced downgrade.
Cover future versions, missing runtime, probe failure, replay, stale identity, races and recovery. No NewAPI/server mutations or universal-future-compatibility claims.

requirements.statement: Use the Windows-compatible Tauri build invocation after frozen pnpm and locked Cargo gates pass, then produce the unsigned private NSIS artifact without changing runtime or dependency resolution.
acceptance: The workflow preserves pnpm install --frozen-lockfile and cargo test --locked before the Tauri build step.
The Windows Tauri build invocation uses the candidate config and NSIS bundle without the PowerShell-incompatible redundant trailing -- --locked argument.
The same clean run passes 136 current renderer tests and all platform-applicable native tests before producing and uploading the unsigned installer.
The final per-artifact receipt proves exact hashes, source commits, architectures and security limitations without any runtime, server, database, updater or public-release change.

requirements.statement: Make the installation-selection core's cfg(test) path fixtures portable so the unchanged production logic is verified with native absolute-path semantics on both macOS and Windows before packaging.
acceptance: All tool_selection_core tests construct native absolute paths through a platform-aware test helper; relative and empty-path rejection remains explicit.
Only cfg(test) code changes in tool_selection_core; production Inventory, bundle classification, deduplication, bounds and selection code remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
The clean Windows workflow passes all 136 selected renderer tests and every platform-applicable locked native test before building the unsigned x64 NSIS installer.
The final receipt records per-artifact source commits and exact hashes and states that RU-021 changed tests only, not production runtime, server, database, updater or release authority.

requirements.statement: Use the current frozen 野菜 product tests, not obsolete inherited upstream App tests, as the Windows renderer gate; retain full native tests and finish the unchanged runtime's Windows internal artifact.
acceptance: The manual Windows workflow explicitly executes all current candidate, diagnostics, configuration, service-catalog, billing and workbench Vitest files and excludes release and inherited work trees; it does not execute obsolete tests/integration/App.test.tsx.
The shared conditional matchMedia test polyfill remains in force and the exact current renderer selection passes with no failed tests before packaging.
The workflow also runs cargo test --locked and builds an unsigned x64 NSIS internal installer only after both renderer and native gates pass.
A replacement receipt binds the resulting Windows installer and retained notarized universal macOS DMG to exact evidence without any runtime, server, database, updater or public-release change.

requirements.statement: Repair only the cross-platform renderer test harness exposed by the clean Windows runner, then produce and bind the unsigned Windows x64 installer alongside the already accepted universal macOS artifact without changing runtime behavior or any server boundary.
acceptance: The shared jsdom setup provides matchMedia only when the environment omits it and exposes the listener methods required by the appearance hook without changing application runtime source.

The existing manual private Windows 2022 workflow completes locked renderer and Rust tests, builds one unsigned x64 NSIS installer, uploads only a private workflow artifact, and creates no tag, release, updater artifact or signing claim.
The replacement receipt binds the Windows installer and retained universal macOS DMG to exact hashes, source identity, architecture, signature state and platform-test limitations.
No server, NewAPI, Nginx, database, production, user-tool configuration, application runtime source or public release is changed.

requirements.statement: Package the verified repaired client for Apple Silicon capable macOS and unsigned Windows internal testing, while delivering a version-pinned NewAPI interface-versus-database handoff without changing any server or publishing a release.
acceptance: Build a Developer ID signed and notarized universal macOS application and DMG containing both arm64 and x86_64 executable slices. Exercise the Intel slice on this host and report that native Apple Silicon launch remains untested without an M-series host.

Use a separate manual private-repository Windows 2022 workflow that runs locked tests and builds only an unsigned internal NSIS installer, uploads a workflow artifact, and never creates a tag, release, updater artifact or public download.

Preserve the RU-017 runtime source and all account, DSH, credential, configuration-write, telemetry and updater boundaries; package evidence must bind every delivered artifact to source, architecture, signature state and hash.

Give the server owner a version-pinned endpoint and persistence matrix. Reuse NewAPI users, user_sessions, logs, tokens, pricing/options and top-up/payment records; use Redis only for expiring one-time device authorization state; add no new schema by default and name the exact audit condition that would justify a later migration.
Perform no server, NewAPI, Nginx, database, production, user-tool configuration or public-release mutation.

requirements.statement: Repair native macOS titlebar consistency and automatically resolve standalone-versus-bundled CLI coexistence without asking beginners to choose paths.
acceptance: Transparent native titlebar and fixed light/dark background retain native decorations. Do not force application or OS appearance, so system mode stays automatic.

Version 2 deduplicates canonical aliases, excludes macOS .app internal executables before probing, selects only standalone candidate or unique earliest absolute PATH candidate. Ties and common-only ambiguity remain unresolved with desktop/retry actions. No user installation or configuration changes.

Fixed five-tool closed projection includes independent and bundled counts and selection reason. Only selected candidate probed; never fall back silently after failure. Reject stale/malformed responses. v1 stays unchanged.

Plain four-locale copy distinguishes Codex CLI. Test native selection, React/IPC theme ordering and scan transitions, workbench/cost regression and exact signed notarized local Intel package. No account, DSH, server, updater or public release activation.

requirements.statement: RU-016 packages the existing verified client into a clearly identified local Intel macOS internal-test build without introducing new runtime behavior or treating the incomplete product as ready.
acceptance: Build the current source using the existing candidate Tauri config; verify the bundle identity, version, icon, Intel architecture and Developer ID signature.
Preserve no updater/deep-link authority and no server or NewAPI modifications; retain existing unavailable billing and DSH states.
Keep an isolated dated installer, artifact hashes and a handoff recording tests, precise limitations, signing/notarization status and backend next steps.
Exercise the actual native application on this Intel Mac. Do not claim Windows or Apple Silicon validation or public release.

requirements.statement: RU-015 supplies a truthful, accessible cost-comparison component and an internal normalized receipt validation boundary without activating account or billing network access.
acceptance: Production billing shows unavailable amounts with an explanation and an auditable comparison-method disclosure; it never fills them using mock requests, zeroes or public prices.

The pure receipt verifier checks complete closed structure, account and period identity, freshness, unique rows, settled and excluded cohort membership, normalized quantities and prices, immutable price metadata, fixed USD-to-CNY 6.75 conversion, sum consistency and decimal integer arithmetic before calculating differences.

Official comparable totals and corresponding actual net charges use exactly the same included rows; pending, missing, unverified model or unsupported funding rows are excluded with reasons and coverage, not assigned invented official costs.

Zero official totals omit percentages; zero and negative differences render neutrally or as a higher cost rather than fabricated savings. Tiny amounts do not render a contradictory zero-price percentage.

Actual settled net debit is supplied as ledger evidence, not recomputed from an advertised ratio. The normalized priced lines are supplied by a future server pricing projection; the client stores no price catalog or expression evaluator.

Four-locale UI, full model IDs, breakdown disclosure, partial/unavailable/invalid/expired states, keyboard focus and narrow layouts are tested. The future authenticated producer and its external API schema remain unimplemented.

requirements.statement: The first DSH graphical integration opens the official local interface in the user's browser from the Yeschoy assistant rather than requiring a native or embedded DSH window.
acceptance: The intended beginner journey uses the assistant to launch DSH and opens its official local browser interface without asking the user to type a shell command.
The Yeschoy application remains the installable assistant; the DSH browser interface is not presented as an official native desktop installer and receives no Yeschoy native bridge permissions.

Recording this presentation choice does not enable a launch button or claim automatic configuration before version, process, configuration and credential contracts are separately implemented and verified.

requirements.statement: DSH is a priority integration target whose actual graphical workflow, provider configuration and security boundaries must be investigated before claiming automatic support.
acceptance: Research distinguishes current official graphical capabilities, current client implementation and proposed integration, with primary-source locators and exact-version limitations.
Any implementation obtains its own frozen scope and verifies the selected DSH version, credentials, configuration preservation and platform behavior before showing supported or connected.
Investigation performs no server changes or paid model requests and does not install, launch or configure DSH or access user credentials.

requirements.statement: The client must make official-versus-Yeschoy usage-cost savings visible only through an honest same-usage comparison that can be checked against official pricing and actual billing records.
acceptance: Current unit-price comparisons and historical actual-charge comparisons are distinguished, and unavailable amounts are never replaced with invented savings.
A professional user can trace compared amounts to the same usage, model, applicable official pricing and Yeschoy billing; assumptions and unsupported comparisons remain explicit.
Detailed calculation, settlement, currency, refund, coverage and display semantics remain proposals until their contract and reconciliation evidence are approved in a later implementation unit.

requirements.statement: RU-012 replaces RU-011 visual presentation with the owner-approved compact desktop workbench while preserving truthful runtime capability and network boundaries.
acceptance: Overview shows actual read-only desktop installation results and explicitly unavailable account metrics, never prototype financial, model or connected data.
Primary navigation separates overview, application setup, model catalog and billing; diagnostics, settings and advanced CLI discovery remain available.
Light, dark and system appearance use one token system; font roles use local system sans-serif and monospace IDs without remote font calls; only the theme preference may be stored.
Newest-request guards, complete projection validation, retry and no-write boundaries survive navigation, rerenders and theme changes; unknown scan failures are never shown as app not installed.
Anonymous catalog reads and two-line diagnostics remain explicit user actions; no login, payment, credential, configuration, server, updater or telemetry action is added.
Four-locale parity, keyboard focus, responsive 320px layout, full model IDs and reduced-motion support are covered by tests and visual review.

requirements.statement: RU-011 supersedes the candidate's command-line-first presentation with a branded desktop-application-first beginner experience for Claude Desktop and the Codex desktop surface while preserving truthful client-only, security and server boundaries.
acceptance: The installed application and every bundled installer use an original 野菜API icon rather than the inherited upstream icon, and the icon is declared in the base Tauri bundle configuration for macOS and Windows outputs.

The primary home destination detects exactly Claude Desktop and the Codex desktop surface through bounded local application locations and identifiers, never substitutes a claude or codex command for a desktop application, never returns a complete user path, and rejects stale or structurally incomplete projections.

The default navigation and application cards lead with desktop applications, recognizable app identities, installation state and the next beginner action; command-line discovery remains reachable only as a secondary advanced destination.

The setup destination presents desktop application, line and real public model ID as the visible path and hides Base URL, configuration file and credential implementation details from the primary flow.

Claude Desktop and Codex desktop configuration remain explicitly unverified and unapplied until their separate documented adapters, first-party account boundary, secure credentials and exact-version evidence exist; no detected application is described as connected or configured.

The visual system uses the frozen cool garden palette, clear Chinese-first typography, compact desktop navigation and application-tray signature; keyboard focus, reduced motion and a usable 320 CSS pixel layout are preserved.

Existing anonymous public catalog reads, account and billing unavailable truth, fixed 6.75 comparison FX, diagnostics, disabled configuration writes, inactive telemetry and updater boundaries remain intact, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, production or public-release resource is changed.

requirements.statement: The local macOS candidate does not claim another application's URL protocol, and its release identity, hardened runtime, signature and notarization state are independently verifiable without enabling unfinished features.
acceptance: The source macOS plist declares no URL handlers, document handlers or replacement callback scheme; no new deep-link runtime is added.
Candidate build configuration keeps hardened runtime enabled, updater artifacts disabled and private credentials absent.

The rebuilt actual app has the expected identity and architecture and no inherited URL handler; final signed artifact verification and honest notarization status are recorded separately from source tests.

requirements.statement: RU-008 provides pnpm-compatible read-only semantic acceptance for the unchanged current client and prepares a signed local macOS candidate without claiming notarization, public release or backend-dependent readiness.
acceptance: Registered read-only-source semantic acceptance covers the actual runtime modules and React state transitions without requiring npm layout or changing pnpm dependencies.
Local signed macOS app/bundle output is separately checked for identity, hardened runtime, contents, hashes and honest notarization status; no installer upload or public release.

requirements.statement: RU-007 supplies a real anonymous first-party model/group catalog and protocol-aware five-tool preview plus an implementable backend handoff while server, credential, account and configuration-write authority remain absent.
acceptance: Only explicit user action can request the three fixed GET paths on one compiled HTTPS origin; no custom URLs, redirects, auth headers, cookies, raw upstream errors, expressions or persisted metadata reach the renderer.

Public catalog facts are labelled non-user-specific; groups are independent of network lines; models retain real IDs and declared protocols while installation compatibility, group-specific stream restrictions and account authorization remain unverified.
Line changes, refreshes and unmounts invalidate prior requests and selections; malformed, partial and failed responses never fall back to sample models, default ratios or cached authentication.

Claude Code requires declared anthropic, Codex requires openai-response, OpenCode and Pi require openai for this preview profile; DSH continues to abstain. Missing declarations block the corresponding preview without claiming that a positive declaration proves real compatibility.

No balance or actual account price is fabricated. Server display exchange rate and fixed 6.75 official comparison FX are distinct. No numeric price projection or client expression execution is introduced.

Bootstrap absence, transport failure, unsupported contract and recognized contract are distinguishable; recognition cannot activate login or apply. The backend handoff includes schema, examples, actual deployed-source evidence, missing services and server-owned acceptance.
Existing candidate regression plus new contract, protocol, race/recovery, UI and handoff tests pass; current native suite compiles and runs without skipped tests.

requirements.statement: The current candidate branch and nightly schedule execute the same bounded read-only-source CI checks with explicit Windows x64 and macOS Intel/Apple Silicon native results, rejecting empty/stale/skipped test suites without pretending to validate legacy WSL configuration writes or public release.
acceptance: Push and PR to main and product/** trigger candidate checks without path filters silently omitting current changes; manual runs and nightly reuse run the same workflow definition.
Frontend checks execute the existing test:candidate script and RU-005 acceptance, not superseded upstream or historical acceptance suites; package installation is frozen-lockfile.

Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon run Rust formatting, Clippy and current library tests using native temporary directories and current crate identity; no WSL path or old atomic-write selector remains.
A test runner fails for compile errors, missing or ambiguous test artifacts, stale identity, zero tests, missing required candidate cases, test failures, ignored/filtered cases and timeouts.
Workflows use read-only contents permissions, pinned action SHAs, no persisted checkout credentials, no inherited secrets, no release/deployment commands and isolated native caches.
Local semantic tests do not substitute for actual hosted results; the CI guide identifies the old incident, current scopes, native test proof, nightly recovery and release/WSL limitations.

requirements.statement: The client presents itself as the official 野菜API desktop client and guides a novice without requiring knowledge of API keys, base URLs, or configuration-file syntax.
acceptance: A first-time user can reach a ready-to-use supported tool through the guided flow without manually entering a base URL or editing a configuration file.
Advanced technical values remain inspectable without dominating the default flow.

requirements.statement: The target client account flow uses first-party browser authorization and then displays account balance, usage, and recharge entry points.
acceptance: The client never asks the user to choose GitHub or LinuxDo as a desktop-specific login provider.
If the website session is absent, the website performs its normal login before authorization.
The device code is short-lived and single-use, and the client exposes waiting, approved, rejected, expired, cancelled, and network-interrupted states.
Passwords, website cookies, API keys, and final desktop session credentials never appear in an authorization URL.
The website names and revokes authorized devices, and the client obeys revocation on its next online request.
A device code expires after 10 minutes, an access token after one hour, an inactive remembered session after 30 days, and every device requires reauthorization no later than 90 days.
The issued device session contains only the approved current-account read and current-device key-management scopes.
A backend device/authorization contract is specified before this target flow is implemented.

requirements.statement: V1 detects installed instances of Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH and reports installed, not found, configured, needs attention, and unsupported-version states.
acceptance: Every supported tool has an explicit detection contract and version evidence.
Not found is not presented as an error.
An unsupported or ambiguous installation is not modified.

requirements.statement: The guided configuration flow selects a line and model, previews the change, creates an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot, writes only owned fields, validates the result, tests connectivity, and rolls back on failure without retaining backup history.
acceptance: Unrelated user configuration survives a successful change.
A failed write or validation restores the exact pre-operation state.
Concurrent external edits produce a visible conflict instead of a silent overwrite.

requirements.statement: Every material local-configuration change uses an encrypted transaction-scoped rollback snapshot that is removed after success or completed recovery; V1 provides no retained backup history or arbitrary user-invoked restore points.
acceptance: The encrypted temporary snapshot is durably created and bound to the target file identity before the write starts.
Successful validation deletes the snapshot immediately; failed validation restores the exact pre-operation state and deletes the snapshot only after recovery completes.
An interrupted transaction is detected on the next launch and recovery is attempted before another write to the same target.
A recovery failure preserves the unfinished-transaction snapshot and operation identifier until recovery succeeds or the user explicitly abandons it.
Snapshots are never uploaded, retained as history, exposed as arbitrary restore points, or used for cross-device restore.
If the operating-system credential store is unavailable, the write is blocked rather than creating a plaintext snapshot.

requirements.statement: Model selection shows the exact model ID and augments it with compatibility, recommendation, speed/quality positioning, availability, and searchable metadata.
acceptance: The exact model ID is visible and copyable before configuration.
The default list contains only models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool.
An all-models view keeps unavailable entries visible but disabled and explains the reason.
Incompatible models are disabled with a reason rather than silently substituted.
A recommended default never prevents explicit user selection.
A removed or newly unavailable selected model requires a new user choice and is never silently replaced.

requirements.statement: Model cards compare official vendor price and authenticated-user actual 野菜API price using the same unit and currency context, including input, output, cache, tier, group, and source freshness when applicable.
acceptance: The official price includes a source URL and last-verified time.
The actual price reflects the current user's eligible group and pricing version.
CNY per one million tokens is the primary comparable display while the official source currency remains visible.
The initial fixed comparison rate is 1 USD = 6.75 CNY and displays its value, version, and effective date without auto-following short-term market movement.
The fixed comparison rate is never presented as or applied as the server billing rate.
Input, output, cache read, cache write, context tiers, and time tiers are shown separately when they differ.
Image, audio, per-request, and other non-token billing preserve their native comparable units.
If prices cannot be compared on one basis, the client says so and does not fabricate a discount.
Stale official prices or an unapproved exchange-rate basis suppress savings conclusions.
All client totals are labelled estimates and server billing remains authoritative.

requirements.statement: The client exposes a mainland-optimized line rooted at https://yeschoy.com and a Cloudflare global-acceleration line rooted at https://api.yeschoy.com, with the effective tool endpoint visible in advanced details.
acceptance: The labels and root endpoints match the accepted line decision.
Protocol-specific path rules are applied by each tool adapter rather than stored as a misleading universal suffix.
The selected effective endpoint is inspectable before configuration.

requirements.statement: Diagnostics distinguish installation, configuration, DNS/TLS/network, authentication, balance, model availability, protocol compatibility, and upstream-service failures and offer safe repair actions.
acceptance: Diagnostics never send prompt or project contents.
Every repair action previews affected files and creates an encrypted temporary rollback snapshot when it changes local state.
A failed diagnosis is reported as unknown rather than a guessed cause.

requirements.statement: Account session credentials, relay API keys, local tool configurations, logs, temporary rollback snapshots, and updater trust are separated by purpose and protected according to their sensitivity.
acceptance: Account-session credentials are never written into a tool configuration.
A desktop session cannot change identity, payment, group, other-device, or administrative state and cannot retrieve another device's complete tool key.
Logout, device revocation, absolute expiry, inactivity expiry, and refresh failure clear the local account session without silently deleting independent tool keys.
Secrets are redacted from logs, analytics, crash reports, and screenshots generated by diagnostics.
Automatic telemetry accepts only schema-validated allowlisted fields and rejects unknown or oversized fields at both client and first-party ingestion boundaries.
Updates are accepted only after cryptographic signature verification against a pinned application key.
Remote authorization content has no privileged desktop IPC access.

requirements.statement: The client displays balance and usage and opens the existing first-party wallet page in the system browser for recharge during V1.
acceptance: Balance and usage identify freshness and retry state.
Recharge does not embed payment credentials or duplicate payment settlement in the client.
Password, email, payment data, recharge-record mutation, and other sensitive account actions remain on the first-party website.
The external wallet destination is restricted to the configured first-party origin.

requirements.statement: V1 does not download, install, update, or uninstall third-party AI tools.
acceptance: A missing tool receives installation guidance only.
No V1 action elevates privileges to install a third-party tool.

requirements.statement: The current product phase remains client-only and produces a separate future NewAPI change specification without applying backend or production changes.
acceptance: No NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, or production configuration is modified in this phase.
Backend-dependent capabilities remain visibly specified or unavailable rather than simulated as complete.

requirements.statement: The two official lines share account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; the client measures their network behavior, recommends one, permits override, and never silently rewrites an already configured line.
acceptance: The same account credential, tool key, model choice, and price projection work across both configured line roots.
Recommendation uses comparable measurements and does not oscillate on a transient result.
Changing an already configured tool to another line requires user confirmation and the normal temporary-rollback transaction.

requirements.statement: Model facts have explicit owners: NewAPI live data owns current-account availability, exact IDs, the numeric official-price baseline, and actual user pricing; a versioned first-party catalog owns compatibility, recommendations, descriptions, and any price provenance metadata not yet returned by NewAPI, but never a duplicate price number.
acceptance: No client-side fuzzy match changes an exact server model ID.
A newly available model without catalog metadata remains identifiable but is not declared compatible without evidence.
The client derives both comparison values from NewAPI's pricing semantics and never embeds an independently maintained numeric official-price table.
The bundled catalog is covered by the signed client artifact and may supplement source and verification metadata until a versioned server contract supersedes it.
NewAPI model_ratio, model_price, and base billing expressions remain vendor official prices; discounts and promotions are represented only by separately identifiable group or special billing rules.
Automatically imported aggregator or channel prices cannot overwrite an official baseline until they are verified against the corresponding vendor source.
Tiered expressions, per-request prices, media units, current-user groups, and special pricing rules are preserved rather than reduced to a universal multiplier formula.

requirements.statement: Relay API keys are isolated by account, device, and tool and are created or reused idempotently without changing when the selected line or model changes.
acceptance: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH on one device never share a relay key with one another.
Repeated configuration, model switching, and line switching reuse the same account-device-tool key.
A second device receives distinct keys so that usage and revocation remain attributable.
The desktop session can manage only keys owned by its own device and never receives another device key's complete plaintext.
A reinstall that cannot securely recover the prior device identity creates a new device identity and does not silently revoke old keys.
Logging out preserves tool keys, while revoking a device cascades to every tool key owned by that device.
A tool-key rotation revokes the old key only after a temporary rollback snapshot is created and the replacement configuration is written, read back, and connectivity-tested successfully.
Removing local configuration requires a separate explicit choice before its remote key is revoked.
Only the fields required by a target tool receive the relay key, and the complete key is never written to logs, diagnostics, analytics, or crash reports.

requirements.statement: V1 has an explicit tested platform matrix: Windows 10 22H2 x64 and Windows 11 x64, plus macOS 13 and later as a Universal Intel and Apple Silicon build; Windows 11 ARM64 x64-emulation is best-effort and not an official release blocker.
acceptance: Release qualification runs on Windows 10 22H2 x64, supported Windows 11 x64 versions, macOS 13 Intel, and macOS 13 or later Apple Silicon.
The macOS artifact is a signed Universal binary containing Intel and Apple Silicon architectures.
Windows WebView2 absence is detected and resolved through the official Microsoft runtime path.
Windows 10 users receive a plain-language operating-system end-of-support warning without being falsely told the client itself is unsupported.
Windows 11 ARM64 x64-emulation defects are documented as best-effort compatibility and do not block V1 unless promoted by a later accepted decision.

requirements.statement: macOS V1 is distributed from the first-party website as a Developer ID-signed and notarized Universal DMG using the existing individual membership, without a Mac App Store listing or an anonymity promise.
acceptance: The public DMG and contained app pass Developer ID signature verification and Apple notarization checks before publication.
The public download origin is first-party and the app update trust chain is independent from transport security alone.
V1 has no Mac App Store product page under the individual legal name.

The website and normal client UI do not proactively publish the signer's personal legal name, while documentation never claims the package is anonymous or that certificate inspection cannot identify the signer.
Unsigned or ad-hoc-signed macOS artifacts remain internal-only.

requirements.statement: Windows and macOS are developed in parallel, but macOS may publish first and Windows remains internal-only until it has trusted signing under a preferred organization or accepted personal publisher identity.
acceptance: No unsigned or self-signed Windows package is offered through a public novice-user download path.
The macOS public release does not wait for unresolved Windows signing if its own release unit is otherwise complete.
Windows direct signing and Microsoft Store MSIX are evaluated against configuration-file access, update behavior, signing identity, and support burden before one is selected.
A personal Windows publisher identity is permitted only as an explicit fallback and is not described as anonymous.
Public release artifacts and update metadata use consistent signing identities so trust does not reset unnecessarily between versions.

requirements.statement: V1 uploads first-party basic operational telemetry by default only after conspicuous notice, allows disabling it without loss of core functionality, and enforces a strict data allowlist that excludes user content and secrets.
acceptance: No telemetry leaves the device before the first-run notice is shown.
Disabling telemetry stops future event and crash-envelope upload, deletes the local pending queue, and leaves login, billing, configuration, diagnostics, and model use functional.
The event schema permits only app, OS, architecture, tool, adapter, operation, line class, model ID, duration, anonymous error, sanitized crash, and rotating pseudonymous telemetry-ID fields.

Account IDs, authorization device IDs, relay keys, prompts, responses, project or configuration content, complete paths, OS usernames, clipboard data, and raw memory dumps are never automatically uploaded.
Crash stacks are normalized and scrubbed locally before upload, and raw diagnostic materials require a separate user-initiated preview and send action.
No third-party analytics SDK may independently collect or expand telemetry fields.

Ordinary events expire after 30 days, sanitized crash events after 90 days, irreversibly de-identified aggregate trends after 12 months, telemetry IDs rotate every 30 days, and local pending uploads expire after seven days.
Disabling telemetry clears pending local events and offers a raw historical-event deletion request; any incident-specific extension records scope, reason, approver, and deletion date.

requirements.statement: The client directly forks CC Switch as its technical foundation while preserving required notices, auditing dependency licenses, maintaining reviewed upstream provenance, and replacing the provider-centric product layer with the confirmed 野菜API experience and security boundaries.
acceptance: The distributed product retains the CC Switch MIT license and copyright notice and has a recorded dependency-license audit.
Reused adapters and file operations pass the 野菜API tool-version, ownership, secret, conflict, and temporary-rollback contracts before they are declared supported.
Provider-centric screens and persistent backup-history behavior are not exposed as the V1 novice experience.
First-party account, billing, authorization, key, pricing, diagnostics, and telemetry modules have explicit boundaries from upstream-derived configuration code.
Every merged upstream change is reviewed and tested; no automatic upstream merge reaches a release branch.

requirements.statement: The stable application identifier is com.yeschoy.desktop across macOS packaging, Windows identity, operating-system credential namespaces, local application data, and signed update channels.
acceptance: Forked CC Switch identifiers are removed or explicitly migrated before any public artifact is built.
macOS bundles, Windows packages, credential-store entries, local application-data roots, telemetry application identity, and update metadata consistently use com.yeschoy.desktop.
Beta and stable channels remain cryptographically and operationally separable without changing the product's stable root identity.
Any future identifier migration requires a separate accepted migration decision and tested credential, data, and updater transition.

requirements.statement: Claude Code and Codex receive the current device's per-tool relay key through a tool-native credential-helper contract backed by the operating-system credential vault, without storing the complete key in their ordinary configuration or official-login cache.
acceptance: Claude Code configuration uses a verified apiKeyHelper path and contains no complete 野菜 relay key.
Codex configuration uses a verified model-provider auth.command path and contains no complete 野菜 relay key in config.toml or auth.json.
The helper reads only the requested account-device-tool credential and never logs, persists, copies, or emits it outside the requesting tool's standard output.
External ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY values that outrank Claude apiKeyHelper are detected or reported as an explicit override rather than misreported as a healthy 野菜 configuration.
An unavailable operating-system credential vault or unsupported tool version blocks configuration and never triggers a plaintext fallback.
The helper packaging and path remain valid after signed install, app update, app relocation scenarios in scope, and Windows or macOS restart.
The minimum supported Claude Code and Codex versions are established by executable configuration and tool-level request tests on every official platform target.

The renderer receives only closed update status, version, notes and byte counts through dedicated IPC; it receives no signing key, artifact path, raw endpoint error or direct updater-plugin authority. Update serialization is independent of tool activation, application installation, account, model and vendor-download state.

The release configuration embeds only the updater public key, creates updater artifacts for candidate builds, keeps the private key outside the repository and public origin, and replaces the inherited CC Switch release identity with Yeschoy-specific manual publication inputs.

The download origin serves an atomically published stable manifest when present and empty HTTP 204 when absent. Immutable versioned artifacts are published before the manifest, rollback disables the manifest without deleting old objects, and health truthfully reflects channel publication.

Happy, failure, replay, stale-version, race and recovery scenarios pass together with renderer, native and publisher tests. A first updater-aware build is identified as the one-time manual bootstrap boundary rather than claiming older clients can discover an updater they do not contain.
